title: Deferred provisioning cooldown safeguard and pulse attenuation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: A production capacity incident on 2026-01-28 caused a sustained tail-latency spike for inference-hosted routes when autoscaling failed to provision in time for a burst. Symptoms included: HPA/KEDA did not scale up quickly for burst cohorts, warm-pool resequencing raced with probe-based scale decisions, and several tenants observed cold-start induced latency > 2x SLO. Root cause analysis indicates a combination of (1) a recent metrics aggregation change that introduced percentile smoothing bias at the controller (false-negative scale signals), (2) an overly aggressive scale-down cooldown that discarded early ascent signals, and (3) probe gating logic that prioritized a single noisy metric rather than a fused signal. This ticket captures the follow-up action plan and implementation steps to reduce false negatives/positives and prevent similar cold-start capacity regressions.
actions: Instrument and ship a deferred-provisioning cooldown safeguard: hold scale-down decisions for a configurable grace window (default 90s) when high-percentile latency or queue depth variance spikes are detected.
Implement pulse attenuation: apply EWMA smoothing on high-frequency scaler inputs and cap instantaneous influence from single-sample spikes. Expose smoothing alpha per-cluster and per-workload.
Cohort-aware warm-pool resequencing: tag warm pools by route cohort and maintain minimum per-cohort capacity to avoid resequencing races during multi-tenant bursts.
Multi-signal probe voting: combine latency p95, queue depth, and request rate with a voting threshold to avoid single-metric noise-driven scale decisions.
Telemetry & alerting: add a dashboard for scale-decision entropy, missed-scale events, and warm-pool contention; alert on sustained missed-scale rate > 0.5%/hour.
Canary rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of clusters with runtime-1.24; autoscaler dry-run mode first, then active scaling with extended logging.
Regression tests & chaos: add synthetic burst tests in CI plus a periodic chaos job that replays production traffic envelopes against autoscaler logic.
Cost guardrails: add a transient overprovision budget per-customer to limit cost exposure during adaptive pre-warming.
Documentation: update runbooks and incident response playbooks to include new metrics and mitigation steps for scale miss scenarios.
tradeoffs: Short-term increased cost from larger transient warm-pools and deferred scale-down windows.
Longer path to reclaim unused capacity vs improved SLO adherence; tradeoff accepted for high-customer-impact routes.
Complexity in autoscaler config surface (alpha/beta knobs) requiring clear sane defaults and console UX to avoid misconfiguration.
acceptance_criteria: Canary clusters show >50% reduction in missed-scale events during synthetic bursts compared to baseline.
No customer-facing latency regressions attributable to the change after 2 weeks of rolling canary.
Dashboard surfaces missed-scale metric and on-call playbook references for at least one SRE runbook review.
